item.title: Net FDI inflows in first half hit four-year high
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Net FDI inflows in first half hit four-year high Investment: Predictable business environment stressed Net foreign direct investment inflows into China reached the highest first-half level in four years, reflecting growing foreign investor confidence as the Chinese economy shifts toward more resilient growth driven by innovation and domestic demand, according to an official, experts and executives. China recorded net FDI inflows of $60.9 billion in the first half of 2026, up 81 percent year-on-year, according to the latest balance of payments data released by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. An administration official confirmed that the figure was the highest for the corresponding period in four years. "In the first half of 2026, foreign direct equity investment totaled $63.8 billion, up 55 percent year-on-year, indicating that FDI inflows into China are stabilizing and gaining momentum," the administration official said. Within foreign direct equity investment, inflows of new capital, which reflect long-term investment intentions, rose 10 percent to $43.1 billion in the first half, the official said. Furthermore, reinvestment of earnings by foreign-invested enterprises in China increased 31 percent. This indicated that they were using more of their earnings to expand investment with a stable willingness to invest and operate here, the official said, adding that "China's steady expansion of institutional opening-up and improvements to its foreign investment services have helped create a favorable development environment for foreign investors to invest and operate in China". "Combined with its vast market, comprehensive industrial system and strong supporting capabilities, these advantages have enabled foreign-invested enterprises to earn relatively high returns, consistently ranking among the highest across major economies," the official said. According to the first-half balance of payments data released by the administration, FDI returns in China came in at $179.8 billion in the first half of 2026, remaining stable compared with the same period last year. Amid persistent global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, executives said China's relatively stable growth and pursuit of high-quality development have provided foreign companies with sources of confidence and opportunity, citing the nation's role as an innovation hub and the growth opportunities offered by its vast domestic market. Australian wine company Treasury Wine Estates said it will continue to deepen its focus on the Chinese market as its flagship Penfolds brand gains momentum in China. "The Chinese mainland is one of the world's most dynamic luxury beverage markets," said Wu Mingfeng, managing director for China at Treasury Wine Estates. Iris Cui, vice-president of Asia procurement and operations at Apple, said that more than 80 percent of Apple's 200 major suppliers worldwide operate manufacturing facilities in China, while work on its newest product — the iPhone Duo — was carried out exclusively in China, from early-stage product development to final assembly. New capital contributions by foreign direct investors into high-tech services and high-tech manufacturing saw a 61 percent year-on-year increase in the first half, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange said in the latest balance of payments report, indicating that foreign investors are shifting from seeking the cost and scale advantages of "Made in China" to participating in "Created in China". The administration official said that FDI under the balance of payments framework, in line with international standards, comprises three components: capital contributions in forms such as funds, physical assets and technology; retained earnings attributable to foreign-invested companies, also known as reinvestment of earnings; and debt transactions with overseas affiliates, which can serve a long-term investment function. All three components are measured on a net basis, deducting withdrawals or repayments from new investment, the administration official said. As for debt transactions, foreign-invested enterprises in China repaid $2.9 billion in loans to overseas affiliates in the first half, down 62 percent year-on-year, the official said, attributing the decline to changes in domestic and overseas financing costs and companies' efforts to optimize funding arrangements. Pan Yuanyuan, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' National Institute for Global Strategy, said, "Taken together, foreign investor confidence has strengthened in the first half." Pan estimated that, based on aggregate macroeconomic data, returns on FDI in China currently range from about 9 to 10 percent, still high globally yet lower than two or three decades ago amid intensified competition. She underscored the need for drawing on China's institutional strengths to further provide a predictable business environment for foreign investors. Looking ahead, the administration official said the administration plans to introduce further measures to facilitate cross-border investment and financing by multinational companies, providing more convenient and efficient services for them. The administration plans to continuously improve cross-border cash-pooling policies, thereby making it easier for multinational companies to pool and manage their renminbi and foreign currency funds across domestic and overseas operations. Other planned measures include simplifying capital-account foreign exchange conversion and payment procedures, refining macroprudential policies on cross-border financing to better meet foreign-invested enterprises' funding needs, and streamlining capital-account registration through greater use of bank services and online processing, the official said.

item.title: Investment demand fuels China's gold buying
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Investment demand fuels China's gold buying Households viewing physical bullion as safe-haven asset, store of wealth Shoppers crowd jewelry counters during major Chinese holidays, yet a noticeable shift is unfolding across retail outlets nationwide: sparkling gold ornaments are losing ground to plain gold bars and coins. For ordinary households, gold is evolving from a festive gift or fashion statement into a favored store of household wealth. For Fu Hao, a 35-year-old marketing manager in Beijing, the calculation has entirely changed. While he once purchased intricately designed gold bracelets for family milestones, he now opts for unadorned bullion. "The premiums you pay for jewelry craftsmanship just aren't worth it anymore," Fu said shortly after purchasing a 50-gram investment bar at a local bank. "We want our purchases to hold their pure value. It may not be wearable, but a plain gold bar provides real peace of mind." This retail trend mirrors a far-reaching strategic shift, according to a recent report by S&P Global. Far from a short-term rush, China's growing engagement with gold spans household asset allocation, domestic mining expansion, central bank reserve building, cross-border financial infrastructure, and outbound resource investment — all unfolding against a broader wave of gold accumulation across emerging economies. Chinese buyers are re-prioritizing gold bars and coins over decorative jewelry, with many families now viewing physical gold as an alternative safe-haven asset, according to the industry data released by the China Gold Association. This structural divergence is becoming increasingly pronounced. According to the CGA, China's gold consumption reached 511.41 metric tons in the first half of 2026, up 1.23 percent year-on-year. However, demand for gold jewelry plummeted 33.88 percent to 132.13 tons, while robust investment demand pushed the consumption of gold bars and coins to 339.34 tons, surging 28.42 percent. Periodic price pullbacks have consistently stimulated sales of gold bars through domestic banking channels, cementing them as a popular hedge against market risks. "This demand cannot be suppressed, even with gold prices at historical highs," said Zhao Xiangbin, chief strategist at Beijing Gold and Forex Fortune Investment Management. "Investor anxieties about geopolitical situations and tariff wars have intensified, leading to a gold market rush to balance asset portfolios and hedge against risks," he said. This consumer phenomenon is not unique to China. S&P Global data point to similar patterns across emerging markets: retail investors are cutting spending on ornamental gold while lifting investment-grade gold purchases when geopolitical and domestic economic risks rise.

item.title: Visitors flock to Shaanxi for its natural beauty
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
"The scenery is stunning," Ilia Popov, 25, a Russian pursuing postgraduate studies at a university in Xianyang, Northwest China's Shaanxi province, exclaimed when taking in the majesty of the Ganquan Canyon. "It's like a painter has drawn his brush across the stone." Located in Ganquan county, Yan'an, Shaanxi province, the Ganquan Canyon is a slot canyon tucked away on the Loess Plateau, earning it the nickname of China's equivalent to the Antelope Canyon in Arizona, the United States. Yan'an is also renowned for its Red tourism. Carved from red sandstone over tens of millions of years through wind erosion, water dissolution and scouring, the Ganquan Canyon is a unique kind of landscape, known as a Danxia landform. It consists of more than 120 gorges, each with distinctive features. Among the most well-known is Huashugou Gorge. It stretches about 1,100 meters, soaring to over 20 meters at its highest point, with widths ranging from one to two meters. Its narrowest point at the floor of the gorge is just 20 centimeters. Popov made his way through the gorge — wide at first, before narrowing gradually until, at its deepest point, allowing only one visitor to pass at a time. Back home, he posted the photos on social media, where his friends commented that the scenery looked like a scene straight out of a sci-fi film. The canyon first captured widespread public attention through stunning images shared online by photographers about a decade ago. In 2017, the Ganquan Canyon scenic area was established and opened to the public. It received 38,000 visitors during the recently concluded National Day holiday. No one knows its gorges better than Yan Dong, a 62-year-old photographer based in Xi'an, Shaanxi, who devoted himself to exploring the Ganquan Canyon between 2015 and 2021. Yan recalled that in 2015, several of the gorges were only known among local villagers and photographers, and he resolved to fully explore the canyon. He braved wild conditions, sought guidance from elderly local villagers and plotted his routes on maps. At the peak of his explorations, he visited the site more than 100 times in a single year. He said he had personally explored more than 30 gorges in the Ganquan Canyon — all previously unknown to outsiders — photographed them and published a photography album of his work. "Something seemed to draw me deeper into exploring the canyon, as if I were on a mission," Yan said. The endeavor was not without risks. He suffered several accidents and injuries, but he never gave up. "Every gorge has its own soul. To others, they may look similar, but to me, each one is different, as if they were my own children. Within each gorge, every section and every spot is distinctive, each yielding unique photographic opportunities," Yan said. The most vibrant colors appear at midday, when sunlight streams into the gorges, he said. "If you visit the day after it rains, the moss is greener and the red sandstone takes on an even deeper hue. It looks even more spectacular." Yan added that he is proud to have contributed to local tourism through his photography. For conservation purposes, the scenic area only opens about five of the canyon's gorges to the public, with two gorges available each day depending on weather and other conditions on the day. Wu Wenjing, a tour guide based in Yan'an, said that many tourists sign up for one-day tours that depart from the city's downtown, which is more than 80 kilometers away. She added that as Yan'an was the center of the Communist revolution from 1935 to 1948 and the former home of the headquarters of the Communist Party of China, Red tourism sites are also popular destinations, in addition to other natural scenic spots. Wu noted that facilities and services at the scenic area have improved to accommodate a steady rise in visitors to the Ganquan Canyon in recent years. Contact the writers at xulin@chinadaily.com.cn If you go The Ganquan Canyon scenic area sets an adult ticket price of 168 yuan ($25), which covers admission and a mandatory shuttle bus ride. Visitors can drive to the scenic area from Xi'an or Yan'an, both in Shaanxi province. Alternatively, visitors can take a high-speed train from Xi'an to Ganquan North Railway Station, then take a 40-kilometer taxi ride to the scenic area.

item.title: China-EU vehicle trade deal benefits both
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
China-EU vehicle trade deal benefits both The consensus reached by China and the European Union on trade in hybrid and electric vehicles effectively safeguards the interests of Chinese companies and prevents bilateral trade frictions from escalating, the Ministry of Commerce said on Monday. Responding to a media query about discussions on trade in hybrid and electric vehicles during last week's second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism in Beijing, a ministry spokesperson said that both sides held intensive consultations based on mutual respect and equality to address trade differences and each other's concerns. The progress made with regard to trade in hybrid and electric vehicles will help create a stable, predictable and sustainable trade and investment environment, and support the steady, balanced and healthy development of China-EU economic and trade relations, the spokesperson said in an online statement. Regarding hybrid vehicles, China and the EU had agreed on three fundamental principles — respect for market realities, nondiscrimination, and compliance with World Trade Organization rules, the spokesperson added. According to Eurostat, the EU's statistical office, the grouping's imports of hybrid vehicles from China climbed from 107,000 units in 2024 to 302,000 units in 2025. Building on the 2025 level, China and the EU reached an arrangement for upward adjustment to ensure export capacity and stable growth for Chinese automakers, while addressing the legitimate concerns of industries on both sides. The two sides agreed that Chinese products and companies would not face discriminatory treatment, and that quotas allocated to China would be no less favorable than those granted to any other source of EU imports, according to the Commerce Ministry. The two sides also confirmed that the trade arrangement must comply with WTO rules, with China retaining all its rights, including the right to seek dispute settlement and trade compensation, the spokesperson said. On electric vehicles, the spokesperson noted that the two sides achieved a "soft landing" in the countervailing duty case in January, when the EU issued general guidance on price undertakings. The EU will continue to advance procedures for price undertakings by individual automakers, as well as other review procedures related to the case. Tian Dewen, a researcher of international relations at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences in Beijing, said the latest consensus marks a further step toward a more institutionalized approach to resolving China-EU automotive trade disputes. Yan Shaohua, deputy director of Fudan University's Center for China-Europe Relations in Shanghai, said that by addressing trade differences through consultation, China and the EU can provide Chinese automakers in Europe with greater regulatory clarity and reduce market uncertainty. Haley Chen, general manager of the Southwest China Chapter of the European Union Chamber of Commerce in China, said the continued dialogue and follow-up engagement between China and the EU will remain essential to strengthening bilateral economic and trade cooperation. Speaking at a news conference in Beijing on Monday ahead of next week's 19th Europe-China Business and Technology Cooperation Fair in Chengdu, Sichuan province, Chen said that there remains considerable potential for mutually beneficial cooperation. "European companies bring expertise in advanced technologies, engineering, precision manufacturing, quality management and sustainable solutions," she said. "China offers a large market, strong industrial capabilities, extensive supply chains and a rapidly developing innovation ecosystem."

item.title: Rebuilt port opens to boost connectivity
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Rebuilt port opens to boost connectivity The redeveloped Huanggang Port, a round-the-clock boundary crossing between Shenzhen in Guangdong province and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, operated smoothly on its opening day with faster clearance for passengers and vehicles, boosting officials' confidence in managing peak traffic during weekends and public holidays. The new port, which opened at 6:30 am on Monday, uses a "collaborative inspection and joint clearance" model, meaning that travelers only need to present their travel documents once to cross the border, while drivers can complete the inspection in one-stop lanes without leaving their vehicles. During its first two hours of operation, the port handled more than 5,000 passengers and nearly 1,000 vehicle trips. Chris Tang Ping-keung, secretary for security of the Hong Kong SAR government, said that between 6:30 am and 8:30 am, the new port recorded 5,170 passenger trips, up by more than 60 percent from the same period on ordinary days. There were also 953 inbound and outbound vehicle trips, about 30 percent more than usual. The port is equipped with 134 "collaborative inspection" self-service channels, 68 traditional manual counters and 28 joint inspection lanes for vehicles. He said that all clearance channels were operating normally and that passengers could cross without waiting. Vehicles using the joint one-stop lanes waited for less than five minutes. Mable Chan, secretary for transport and logistics of the Hong Kong SAR government, said that by 8 am, 1,200 public transport passengers had crossed northward through Huanggang Port, while nearly 2,000 had traveled south. Eric Chan Kwok-ki, chief secretary for administration of the Hong Kong SAR government, said he was confident that, after a few days of familiarization with the procedures, staff members would be able to handle greater passenger flows during the Chongyang Festival, also known as the Double Ninth Festival, a traditional Chinese occasion honoring senior citizens, which falls on Sunday. He added that if the arrangement proved effective, the authorities would consider extending the clearance model to other ports. A Shenzhen resident surnamed Huang who works in Hong Kong became the first inbound traveler to enter the Chinese mainland through the rebuilt port. Huang, who had just finished her night shift and was returning to Shenzhen, said that it took her only about five minutes to complete the clearance procedures, a significant reduction from the half hour it used to take. Huang said that, with the new port's significantly improved procedures and completely revamped facilities, travel will be much more convenient for cross-boundary commuters. A traveler from the United States who identified himself as Charles visited Shenzhen for business purposes. He used Huanggang Port for the first time on Monday and was satisfied with his experience. Given Huanggang's proximity to downtown Shenzhen, he said he believes that, besides Shenzhen Bay Port, this brand-new port will become another popular choice for international travelers. A cross-boundary coach driver who gave his surname as Tam was the first driver to pass through the new port's joint vehicle inspection channel. After the vehicle entered the inspection lane, it took him just three minutes — and only one stop — to complete document scanning, facial recognition and fingerprint verification, without leaving his vehicle. Previously, he had to stop multiple times for inspections by various parties, which took about 10 minutes. Yolk Lam, a service ambassador stationed at the public transport interchange floor of the port's Hong Kong side, is responsible for handling questions from passengers arriving from Shenzhen and advising them on how to get home. The most frequent and complex inquiries, Lam said, concern direct transport to the airport at Chek Lap Kok, as some passengers may be unsure about the new bus services.

item.title: AI accessibility empowering ordinary people
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
AI accessibility empowering ordinary people Record-breaking Shanghai competition highlights growth of user-friendly coding to prioritize focus on ideas For most children, when summer camp ends, all that remains are photos, journal entries and memories that gradually fade. However, 9-year-old Luo Ange turned a seven-day pottery journey into an online "Clay Lab" that can be accessed and shared at any time. She used an artificial intelligence tool to input natural sentences to help write code and create the online lab, a process known as "vibe coding". Highly praised for its innovative concept, well-thought-out product logic and human touch, the work stood out among over 10,000 competitors to win one of the first prizes at Shanghai's Bund Hackathon AI Coding Competition that ended on Sept 9. Luo's inspiration came from attending a pottery summer camp in the mountains of Ganzhou, Jiangxi province, during the summer holidays. She experienced the entire process of traditional pottery-making, from digging the clay, sifting out impurities, mixing the clay, gathering firewood, loading the kiln, and firing and keeping watch over it. The details sparked an idea. Luo wanted to turn everything she had made, seen and learned into a digital work that can be preserved and shared. After learning about the Bund Hackathon competition, she was encouraged by her father to bring her idea to life. With no coding experience and no existing reference work to consult, she turned to AI tools including ChatGPT and Kimi, using conversational communication and precise requests to build the lab's framework and details. After two days, Luo transformed her concept into an online link. Without the need to download anything or log in, users can simply open their browser to explore the pottery-making experience. The lab faithfully follows the major steps of the pottery-making process, and features social functions such as visiting friends, sending flowers and saving pottery shards. Luo wants her lab to be seen by a large number of viewers and also act as a tribute to the work of the summer camp organizers. She also hopes it will help connect more of her peers. The Clay Lab has no scores, rankings, rewards or punishments, as Luo sees no right or wrong answers in creativity. In her online pottery museum, even pieces that failed to fire properly or are imperfect are on display. It's not the first time Luo tried to use AI for creative work. Through trial and error she learned about communicating, collaborating and iterating with AI, honing her logical thinking and problem-solving skills. "AI is more like a friend I can communicate with and work with. When the AI produces errors or the content is off, I patiently point out the issues, communicate with it and make adjustment to refine it bit by bit," said Luo.

item.title: The Long March inspires generations to keep going further
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
The Long March inspires generations to keep going further When the Central Red Army set out from Yudu, Jiangxi province, in 1934, no one knew what lay ahead. When the world-famous Long March (1934-36) finally came to an end, they could hardly have imagined what this strategic shift would come to mean to generations of Chinese people. Ninety years after the victory, China Daily reporter Yan An retraced the route, returning to places where the Red Army once battled nature and adversity. The snow-covered mountains once crossed by soldiers in straw sandals have become testing grounds for mountaineers challenging their limits. The raging rivers once crossed on makeshift bridges are now spanned by towering modern bridges, including the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge, the world's highest bridge. The landscapes have changed. But the spirit that carried people forward remains. The Long March was a journey that tested the limits of human endurance. Nine decades later, its path has become a starting point for generations to go further — to climb higher mountains, cross deeper waters and overcome new challenges.
